get.description: Answers 204 when the Worker is deployed and serving. Use it for uptime checks; it reads no storage.

post.description: Signs a browser in with the deployment's API token: answers 204 with the sign-in cookie, HttpOnly, Secure and SameSite=Strict, for /api, kept 30 days. The API then accepts it in place of the bearer token. A wrong token answers 401 and sets nothing.
Signs the browser out: answers 204 and removes the sign-in cookie.

get.description: The workspace's projects, by key: each one's key, name, and when it was created.

post.description: Creates a project: one product, with the components that ship separately. Its key is permanent.

get.description: One project and its components, by key.

post.description: Adds a component to a project and returns its ingest key, which its telemetry is sent with. The key is shown only in this answer.

get.description: Every operation in a period, the most counted first, or one with `operation`: how many times it ran, how many failed, and their average, p50, p80, p95 and p99 durations. Counted by the minute for periods of two days or less (kept 14 days), by the hour beyond (kept 15 months); `covered` says which part of the period the counts cover.

The load over a period: how many operations ran and failed, one point per step that had any, with their p50, p80, p95 and p99 durations, on a project's services, or on one operation with `operation`. A step without a point had nothing reported. Past two days the counts are hourly, so a finer step becomes an hour; `step` says which was used.

Traces worth opening in a period, or one operation's with `operation`: the slowest, slowest first, and the failed, newest first, at most 20 of each, each with its ID, which opens it with the traces endpoint. Of each operation, environment and hour, the five slowest traces and the five slowest failed ones are kept, 14 days; `covered` says which part of the period that covers.
The errors of a period, most frequent first: each error log grouped by its exception's type and stack, or by its logger and message, with when it was first and last seen. Kept 90 days.

One error and its latest occurrences in a period, with their messages, stack traces, and trace IDs: where an investigation starts. Each occurrence's trace ID and time open its trace with the traces endpoint.

Warnings and errors, newest first, 100 at a time: filtered by level, text, logger, trace, or error. Kept 90 days. Records below warning are in the archive, which the traces endpoint reads for one trace.

Warnings and errors counted over time: a series for each level, component, or error group (`by`), at `level` or above (warn when absent), with a point for each step that had any. By error group, the 100 most frequent. Kept 90 days; `covered` says which part of the period the counts cover.

One trace across services, from the archive, found by its ID: its spans as a tree, with their durations and attributes, and its logs at every level. `around`, the time it happened, is optional: of a trace with more archive files than are read, those nearest to it are read first. Kept 90 days.

The project's open incidents, newest first, and up to 50 resolved in the last 7 days. Detectors look every minute: a monitor down two checks in a row, an operation failing at least 2% and three times its usual over 15 minutes, and a scheduled operation that missed twice its usual gap. `checkedAt` says when they last looked.

post.description: Marks an incident as being looked at, which stops its notifications, and returns it. Acknowledging it again keeps the first time.

get.description: The project's monitors, oldest first, each with its last check: the URLs fetched every minute, which pass with a status below 400 within 10 seconds.

post.description: Adds a monitor: a URL of one component, such as its health endpoint, fetched every minute from the next check on. A project has at most 20.

delete.description: Removes a monitor, and resolves its open incident, if any.

post.description: Pairs a phone with a code from a pairing link, and answers with its key, shown only this once: the phone calls the API with it as its bearer token, acting for whoever started the pairing, and sends `User-Agent: Cluenori/<app version> iOS/<iOS version>` so the deployment keeps its versions. A code that is wrong, used, or expired answers 403.

get.description: The phones paired with the deployment, the latest paired first, each with its model, iOS and app versions, and when, from which address and country, it last called.

post.description: Starts pairing a phone for whoever calls: the link a phone opens to pair, shown as a QR code, `cluenori://pair?url=<deployment>&code=<pairing code>`, good once for 10 minutes. At most 5 are good at once; another drops the oldest.

delete.description: Removes a phone: its key stops working at once.

put.description: Keeps the push token of the phone whose key is the bearer token, and the APNs environment it belongs to, in place of any before: the phone calls it each time iOS gives the app a token. Any other credential, or a removed phone's key, answers 401.

post.description: Rings a phone with a test alarm, as a project that is down would, and answers 204 once APNs took it. 409 when push isn't set up or the phone has no push token yet; 502 with Apple's reason when APNs refused it, such as for a wrong key; 503 when APNs didn't answer.

get.description: What needs attention now across every project, the most urgent first: open incidents not acknowledged, errors happening now (seen in the last 15 minutes), acknowledged incidents, new errors (first seen in the last day), operations whose p95 over the last day is at least 1.5 times and 100 ms more than over the 7 days before, and projects with components that sent nothing in the last day. Each item has its evidence and its project; `projects` names every project asked; a project that didn't answer is in `unanswered`, its items missing.
